tech stack: Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 WebFlux / Reactive Event-Driven Stream Processing

module_layout.integration: Single deployable. Contexts integrate through in-process bounded reactive event channels (Sinks.many().multicast().onBackpressureBuffer with externalized capacity and overflow strategy): Intake -> Chronology Reconciliation -> Ledger. Consumers only use published events (TelemetrySampleValidated/ValidationFailed, TelemetrySampleOrdered/BackfillDetected, TelemetryRecordAppended); event bridge adapters map transport payloads to typed domain events. External ingress is an open-host WebFlux contract; downstream broadcasting is external and out of scope.

build_order: Telemetry Intake domain and application (boundary validation, VALIDATION_FAILED tagging)
Telemetry Intake api (ingress packet endpoint with backpressure)
Chronology Reconciliation domain and application (60s sliding reorder window by t_device)
Telemetry Record Ledger domain and application (append-only revisions)
Ledger infrastructure (R2DBC repository adapters, entity mappings, data-access config)
Pipeline assembly (subscription beans via SmartLifecycle, event bridges, retry/DLQ sinks)
risks: Samples later than the 60-second window have unspecified policy (open question); needs a configurable late-arrival policy
Unbounded reorder buffers under burst load; must use bounded sinks with declared capacity and overflow strategy
Failed ledger appends must be retried idempotently with backoff and a dead-letter sink
Boundary limits, window duration and buffer capacities must be externalized configuration, not hardcoded
Downstream broadcasting to analytics consumers is undescribed and treated as external
Eventual consistency across contexts: a sample may be validated but not yet stored

drivers: Append-only write throughput from 1Hz streams of many devices
Auditability and immutability of raw records
persistence.storage_paradigm: Relational (SQL) append-only time-series event store, accessed through non-blocking R2DBC
persistence.data_model: Telemetry record revision: device id, metric type, t_device, t_ingress, value, validation status, revision number, revision reason (original/correction/backfill). Records are insert-only; a new revision is appended instead of updating. Uniqueness on (device id, metric type, t_device, revision).
queries: Latest revision per (device, metric, t_device) over a time range
Full revision history of a sample for audit
Range scan by device and t_device
persistence.migration_plan: Versioned expand-only schema migrations run by Flyway at startup; in-process H2 (r2dbc-h2 plus h2 for Flyway JDBC) substitutes the production store for local runs and tests.
persistence.backup_recovery: Periodic snapshots plus point-in-time recovery of the store; append-only history allows replay and reconstruction.
open_questions: Retention and partitioning policy for high-volume time-series data
